title: Cell survival after a dose of radiation
caption: In the linear-quadratic model the surviving fraction is S = e^(−αD − βD²). With α = 0.3 Gy⁻¹ and β = 0.03 Gy⁻², a 2 Gy dose leaves 0.49 of cells surviving. The βD² term bends the curve down at high doses, which is why radiotherapy is split into many small fractions.
alt: Surviving fraction against dose in grays, falling from 1, with 0.49 at 2 gray marked, curving downward more steeply at higher doses.
